statement.p: A rod has length 5 meters. At a distance x meters from its left end, the density of the rod is given by \delta(x)=5 + 5 x g/m.
(a) Complete the Riemann sum for the total mass of the rod (use Dx in place of \Delta x):
(b) Convert the Riemann sum to an integral and find the exact mass.

static.solution:
(a) Suppose we choose an x, 0\leq x\leq 5. If \Delta x is a small fraction of a meter, then the density of the rod is approximately \delta(x) anywhere from x to x+\Delta x meters from the left end of the rod. The mass of the rod from x to x+\Delta x meters is therefore approximately \delta(x) \Delta x = (5 + 5 x)\Delta x. If we slice the rod into N pieces, then a Riemann sum is \Sigma_{i=1}^{N}(5 + 5 x_i)\Delta x, or, more loosely, \Sigma (5 + 5 x)\Delta x.
(b) The definite integral is M=\int_0^{5} \delta(x)\,dx = \int_0^{5} (5 + 5 x)\,dx= (5 x + {5\over2} x^2)\bigg|_0^{5} = {175\over2} \hbox{ grams}.
